summary: Allow a native driver seat to borrow an existing person's terminal without launching or terminating its shell.

replay.detail: No full claim replay or projection migration. Existing member declarations retain their serialized form; bindings and invocation fences persist through ordinary claim loading and daemon restart.

schema.detail: No database schema or index change. New declarations carry an optional terminal_binding member and the terminal-bound lifecycle.

rules.detail: Existing checkpoint rules and digest inputs are unchanged. Only the terminal owner's person actor may publish a new terminal binding; local and replicated claim admission enforce the existing terminal-owner-forbidden rule.

compatibility.detail: Adds bind-terminal to top-level harness seats. Drivers match a bound person's terminal tag and exact PTY incarnation, then use a per-invocation agent fence. Existing managed drivers retain their normal tag lookup. Older binaries cannot read the terminal-bound member lifecycle.

manual.detail: Upgrade the terminal-owning daemon before creating bindings. Callers declare with the person's credential and launch a registered driver as a child of the shell. Terminal PATH shims and user surfaces are separate changes.

recovery.detail: Rollback is supported before bindings have been created. Once bindings exist, roll forward: older reconcilers do not know that stop intents must preserve a borrowed shell. A killed driver that never records its exit may leave the seat observed running while its shell survives.

downtime.detail: Normal daemon restart; interruption duration has not been measured. A bound driver exit remains terminal after daemon restart without respawning the shell.
